Home/Scale Standard

The STLACCESS Scale Standard

One reference locks in every conversion on this site: a 175cm human with eyes at 160cm. Gaming scales measure to eye level. Ratio scales measure to the top of the head. This single convention is why 28mm scales up to 32mm at exactly 114.3% — and why mixing measurement styles without adjusting produces undersized or oversized prints.

Last updated: October 14, 2026

The Direct Answer

The STLACCESS Scale Standard measures every miniature from a 175cm human baseline: eyes at 160cm for gaming scales (28mm, 32mm, 35mm, 40mm, 75mm), the full 175cm crown for ratio scales (1:35, 1:27, 1:48, 1:56, 1:72, 1:100). Slicer percentage = (target standard mm ÷ source standard mm) × 100. All numbers verified on physical FDM test prints.

The three rules

Gaming scales → eye level

28mm, 32mm, 35mm, 40mm, 75mm measure to the eyes: a 175cm human's eyes sit at 160cm. That is the reference for every gaming scale.

Ratio scales → top of head

1:35, 1:27, 1:48, 1:56, 1:72, 1:100 measure to the crown: the full 175cm. 1:48 = 175 ÷ 48 = 36.458mm top of head.

Same baseline, pure ratio

(target ÷ source) × 100. 28 ÷ 32 = 87.5% down; 32 ÷ 28 = 114.3% up. No fudge factors — the percentages come straight from the standard.
